Unknown accused bypassed the digital security lock and forced entry through the rear patio door. The master bedroom was ransacked, and a steel safe was forced open using heavy tools. Stolen items include approximately 250 grams of gold jewelry and Rs. 1.5 Lakhs in cash. Scene of Crime Officers (SOCO) successfully lifted 3 latent fingerprints from the safe's handle. The canine squad tracked a scent to the main highway, indicating the perpetrators likely used a pre-arranged getaway vehicle. CDR (Call Detail Record) analysis of active mobile towers in the vicinity during the timeframe is currently underway to identify suspicious numbers.

U/s 302 IPC (Murder): On the incident date at approximately 23:30 hrs, a PCR call was received regarding a suspicious incident within the station limits. Responding officers found an unresponsive male victim with severe blunt force trauma to the cranium. The victim was pronounced dead on scene by emergency medical personnel. Preliminary crime scene investigation reveals signs of a violent struggle, with defensive wounds on the victim's forearms. A suspected murder weapon, a heavy iron wrench, was recovered 50 meters away in a storm drain. Neighborhood canvas yielded one eyewitness who reported hearing a loud altercation between two individuals. Technical surveillance and CCTV mapping of the surrounding 2km radius have been initiated. Forensic teams have collected blood swabs and DNA evidence for profiling. The investigation is ongoing to trace the suspect's escape route.

U/s 147/324/504 IPC (Rioting and Armed Assault): Control room dispatched units to a severe public disturbance at the main commercial square. Three victims were transported to the district government hospital with deep lacerations and head injuries. Preliminary inquiries suggest the clash originated from a long-standing property dispute between two rival factions. Digital evidence, including multiple smartphone videos recorded by bystanders, has been confiscated for facial recognition analysis to identify the primary instigators.

Panicked, the victim clicked a malicious APK link which silently installed a remote-access trojan (RAT) on their mobile device. The accused bypassed OTP verification by intercepting SMS permissions, successfully siphoning Rs. 4.2 Lakhs across multiple transactions to mule accounts in a different state. The Cyber Crime branch has frozen the destination accounts via the national portal and is currently tracing the IP logs, device signatures, and VPN nodes used by the attackers.

Preliminary crime scene investigation reveals signs of a violent struggle, with defensive wounds on the victim's forearms. A suspected murder weapon, a heavy iron wrench, was recovered 50 meters away in a storm drain. Neighborhood canvas yielded one eyewitness who reported hearing a loud altercation between two individuals. Technical surveillance and CCTV mapping of the surrounding 2km radius have been initiated. Forensic teams have collected blood swabs and DNA evidence for profiling. The investigation is ongoing to trace the suspect's escape route.

U/s 363/384 IPC (Abduction and Extortion): An urgent missing person report was upgraded to kidnapping after the victim's family received a ransom demand of Rs. 10 Lakhs via a VoIP application. The victim, a local business owner, was last seen leaving their shop at 20:00 hrs. Their abandoned vehicle was located with the engine running on the state highway outskirts. The Anti-Extortion Cell (AEC) and a special task force have been mobilized. The kidnappers are utilizing burner devices and routing their internet traffic through proxy servers to mask their physical location. A covert operation is being planned in coordination with telecom nodal officers to triangulate the ping locations. The victim's safety remains the absolute highest priority of the investigative team.

U/s 66D IT Act & 420 IPC (Cyber Fraud): A formal complaint was filed at the CEN unit by a citizen who fell victim to a sophisticated financial phishing syndicate. The accused bypassed OTP verification by intercepting SMS permissions, successfully siphoning Rs. 4.2 Lakhs across multiple transactions to mule accounts in a different state. The Cyber Crime branch has frozen the destination accounts via the national portal and is currently tracing the IP logs, device signatures, and VPN nodes used by the attackers.

The accused bypassed OTP verification by intercepting SMS permissions, successfully siphoning Rs. 4.2 Lakhs across multiple transactions to mule accounts in a different state. The Cyber Crime branch has frozen the destination accounts via the national portal and is currently tracing the IP logs, device signatures, and VPN nodes used by the attackers.

The Anti-Extortion Cell (AEC) and a special task force have been mobilized. A covert operation is being planned in coordination with telecom nodal officers to triangulate the ping locations.
